title: The First Coffee (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational 96bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal life philosophy absurdist family Zimbabwe Perth morning
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The first coffee of the morning is not a preference — it's a position
On the nature of consciousness and what constitutes transition
From the state of sleep to the state of the functional
The first coffee is the bridge between the two — it's constitutional

[Pre-Chorus]
I've had the same first coffee in the same mug for thirty years
And the first coffee has never once changed and never disappears

[Chorus]
The first coffee knows something I don't know yet
It knows the exact temperature at which the day is set
The first coffee doesn't need context or acknowledgement
It just begins the conversation between me and it
That's my boy

[Verse 2]
Wilma takes hers in the garden when the weather is agreeable
And the garden meets the coffee in a way that's unrepeatable
By any other combination of a substance and a place
The first coffee in the garden is a different state of grace

[Bridge]
My father had his first coffee before anyone else was up
Standing at the window in the dark with his particular cup
Watching the Zimbabwe dawn arrive without a word
And I've inherited that habit and the meaning of what he heard
In that particular silence

[Outro]
First coffee knows… the day has not started until it starts it…
That's my boy
